full_text_en:
Aitefu Company v. Beijing Ditan Hospital et al.

Appeal Case Concerning Unfair Competition Dispute

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2002) Min San Zhong Zi No. 1

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Jiangsu Aitefu Pharmaceutical Health Products Co., Ltd. Domicile: Chenqiao Town, Jinhu County, Huaiyin City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Shen Kaicheng, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Ji Dazhu, Attorney at Beijing Huizhong Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Beijing Ditan Hospital. Domicile: No. 13, Ditan Park, Andingmenwai, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Feng Huizhong, President of the Hospital.

Agent ad litem: Wei Daling, Attorney at Beijing Zhongtian Zhongrui Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Feng Jinwei, Attorney at Beijing Haituo Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Jinhu County Aitefu Chemical Co., Ltd. Domicile: Chenqiao Town, Jinhu County, Huaiyin City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Shen Kaicheng, Chairman of the Board.

Defendant at First Instance: Beijing Qingyu Pharmaceutical Sales Department. Domicile: Ground Floor, Building 22, Dongzhong Street, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Feng Qiue, Manager of the Sales Department.

Agent ad litem: Ni Xiaowen, Attorney at Beijing Dacheng Law Firm.

In the case concerning a dispute over unfair competition between the appellant Jiangsu Aitefu Pharmaceutical Health Products Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Aitefu Health Products Company) and the appellee Beijing Ditan Hospital (hereinafter referred to as Ditan Hospital), the defendants at first instance Jinhu County Aitefu Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Aitefu Chemical Company) and Beijing Qingyu Pharmaceutical Sales Department, the appellant appealed against the civil judgment (2001) Gao Zhi Chu Zi No. 79 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court. This Court, in accordance with the law, formed a collegial panel and held a public hearing of the case. The legal representative of the appellant Aitefu Health Products Company, Shen Kaicheng, and his agent ad litem, the agent ad litem of the appellee Ditan Hospital, the agent ad litem of the defendant at first instance Beijing Qingyu Pharmaceutical Sales Department, and the legal representative of the defendant at first instance Aitefu Chemical Company appeared in court for the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

The Beijing High People's Court found the following facts upon trial: In 1984, the predecessor of Ditan Hospital, the First Infectious Disease Hospital of Beijing, developed a disinfectant capable of rapidly killing various types of hepatitis viruses. After expert appraisal organized by the Beijing Municipal Health Bureau, it was awarded the second prize for applied achievements and was named "84" Hepatitis Wash-Disinfectant, later renamed "84 Disinfectant". In March 1985, the Beijing Municipal People's Government awarded Ditan Hospital the third prize for scientific and technological achievements. In 1984, Ditan Hospital established the "Labor Service Company of the First Infectious Disease Hospital of Beijing" to produce and sell "84" Disinfectant. In June 1992, Ditan Hospital contributed capital to establish "Beijing Long'an Medical Technology Development Company" (hereinafter referred to as Long'an Company), commissioning it to produce and sell "84" Disinfectant. The parties agreed that any future legal disputes arising from the production, research, development, and sale of "84" Disinfectant would be handled in the name of Ditan Hospital, with Ditan Hospital taking the lead in resolving them. Ditan Hospital also, in March 1997, through the formation of a group company, transferred and licensed its technology to over thirty manufacturers nationwide, allowing them to produce and sell "84" Disinfectant.

With the increasing recognition of "84" Disinfectant, many counterfeit "84" Disinfectant products appeared on the market, causing market confusion. The Fair Trade Bureau of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce issued Letter No. 26 on May 30, 2000, requesting the investigation and punishment of acts counterfeiting the well-known product "84" Disinfectant.

On August 21, 1987, Ditan Hospital and Jinhu County Organic Chemical Plant (hereinafter referred to as Jinhu Chemical Plant) signed the "Contract on Joint Production of '84' Hepatitis Wash-Disinfectant", which stipulated: the two parties would jointly produce "84" Hepatitis Wash-Disinfectant; Ditan Hospital would provide the technology and train production and testing personnel for Jinhu Chemical Plant; Jinhu Chemical Plant would pay Ditan Hospital RMB 10,000 in scientific research funds, and annually extract 10% of the net profit from this product as Ditan Hospital's share of the joint production profits; Ditan Hospital retained the ownership and right to transfer the technological achievements, with the restriction that it would not further transfer or engage in joint operations within the area north of the Yangtze River in Jiangsu Province and Nanjing City. In October 1999, Jinhu Chemical Plant changed its name to Aitefu Chemical Company.

On July 2, 1992, Jinhu Chemical Plant, with cash, factory buildings, equipment, and trademark exclusive rights, formed a joint venture with Hong Kong Li Qiang Co., Ltd. to establish Aitefu Health Products Company, which produced disinfectants, cleaning, hygiene, and daily chemical products. That same year, the company began producing and selling "84" Disinfectant. From May 1994 to the present, Aitefu Health Products Company has promoted its Aitefu brand "84" Disinfectant through newspaper advertisements, television advertisements, and advertising posters.

Beijing Qingyu Pharmaceutical Sales Department sold "Aitefu Brand 84 Disinfectant" in Beijing, which was sourced from Beijing Anqi Hua'er Pharmaceutical Development Co., Ltd., on a consignment basis.

The Beijing High People's Court held that since its launch on the market in 1985, "84" Disinfectant had gained widespread consumer recognition and had a certain market reputation; it was a product known to the public and should be recognized as a well-known product. The name "84" as a disinfectant was first used by Ditan Hospital and became well-known through the hospital's use. The term "84" was closely associated with Ditan Hospital and the disinfectant it had developed and produced, becoming representative and symbolic of the product. Therefore, "84" had acquired distinctive features that distinguished it from other related products, and should be recognized as the unique name of the disinfectant produced by Ditan Hospital. Although Ditan Hospital was not the producer or operator of the product, because its funding sources were based on differential subsidies, it had the right to entrust others to produce and sell "84" Disinfectant, and this did not affect its capacity as a rights holder to assert its rights. Ditan Hospital lawfully enjoyed the exclusive right to the unique name of the well-known product.

Aitefu Health Products Company, without Ditan Hospital's permission, used "84" Disinfectant as the name of its product, which was sufficient to cause confusion with Ditan Hospital's product and consumer misidentification, constituting unfair competition, and should bear civil liability. Ditan Hospital's allegation that Aitefu Chemical Company transferred the "84" Disinfectant technology to Aitefu Health Products Company lacked factual basis. Beijing Qingyu Pharmaceutical Sales Department purchased "Aitefu Brand 84 Disinfectant" from a legitimate and formal channel and had no fault in this case. Therefore, Aitefu Chemical Company and Beijing Qingyu Pharmaceutical Sales Department should not bear tort liability. Based on the existing evidence, both the amount of Ditan Hospital's losses and the profits gained by Aitefu Health Products Company could not be accurately calculated and confirmed. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's "Minutes of the Symposium on Intellectual Property Trial Work of Some Courts Nationwide" dated July 20, 1998, and considering the specific circumstances of this case, the amount of damages was determined at the court's discretion.

Pursuant to Article 5, Paragraph 1, Item (2) and Article 20, Paragraph 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, the Beijing High People's Court entered the following judgment: 1. Aitefu Health Products Company shall immediately cease using "84" as the product name for the disinfectant it produces and sells, and shall cease advertising under the name "84" Disinfectant in all media; 2. Aitefu Health Products Company shall, within 30 days of this judgment taking effect, publish an apology to Ditan Hospital in the Xinmin Evening News and the Beijing Evening News; 3. Aitefu Health Products Company shall compensate Ditan Hospital for economic losses in the amount of RMB 250,000. The case acceptance fee of RMB 28,010 shall be borne by Ditan Hospital in the amount of RMB 26,066.1 and by Aitefu Health Products Company in the amount of RMB 1,943.9.

Aitefu Health Products Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this Court, arguing: 1. The first-instance judgment's finding that "84" Disinfectant became a well-known product through the appellee's use was a factual error. The appellee failed to provide evidence of how the technology was marketized or its share in the national market for similar products. "84" Disinfectant became well-known due to the appellant's production of "Aitefu Brand '84' Disinfectant". 2. "84" is a generic name for disinfectant products of the same type and should not be recognized as the appellee's unique name. 3. The appellee lacked standing as a plaintiff in this case. Therefore, the appellant requested that the original judgment be reversed and the appellee's claims be dismissed.

Ditan Hospital replied in defense: 1. The product name "84" Disinfectant consists of the generic part "Disinfectant" and the unique part "84", which is significantly distinct from generic names. It is the unique name of the chlorine-containing disinfectant product produced by the appellee, not a generic name for all chlorine-containing disinfectants. 2. "84" Disinfectant has a certain market reputation and is known to the relevant public; it is a well-known product. 3. The appellee lawfully has standing to sue in this case. 4. The appellant, without the appellee's consent, used the unique name "84" for its disinfectant product, constituting unfair competition.

During the second-instance trial of this Court, upon inquiry and pre-trial exchange of evidence, the disputed issues between the parties were confirmed as follows: 1. Did the appellant's or the appellee's business use cause "84" Disinfectant to become a well-known product? 2. Does "84" Disinfectant constitute the unique name of a well-known product? 3. Does Ditan Hospital have standing to sue in this case?

This Court found upon further trial that the facts found by the first-instance court were substantially true, but there were omissions in the case facts that affect the outcome of this case.

This Court additionally found that after the predecessor of Ditan Hospital, the First Infectious Disease Hospital of Beijing, successfully developed "84" Hepatitis Wash-Disinfectant in 1984, it transferred the technology to more than thirty enterprises nationwide. Each transferee enterprise marked its product with its trademark and the name "84" Hepatitis Wash-Disinfectant or "84" Disinfectant. On August 21, 1987, Ditan Hospital also signed the "Contract on Joint Production of '84' Hepatitis Wash-Disinfectant" with Jinhu Chemical Plant, stipulating that Ditan Hospital would provide relevant technical materials, retain ownership and the right to transfer the technological achievements, but within the area north of the Yangtze River in Jiangsu Province and Nanjing City, further transfer or joint operations were not permitted; Jinhu Chemical Plant would pay RMB 10,000 in scientific research funds and annually extract 10% of the net profit from this product as Ditan Hospital's share of the joint production profits, to be settled in December of each year. This joint production contract only specified the ownership of the technical achievements of "84" Hepatitis Wash-Disinfectant, without specifying other intellectual property rights or ownership of the product. On March 14, 1988, Jinhu Chemical Plant, in accordance with the contract, paid Ditan Hospital RMB 10,000 as a technology transfer fee and began mass production of "84" Disinfectant. Ditan Hospital, Jinhu Chemical Plant, and several other enterprises formed a loose "84" Pharmaceutical Equipment Group to promote and market the production technology of "84" Disinfectant, expanding the product's market sales. In February 1990, Jinhu Chemical Plant paid Ditan Hospital RMB 2,310 as a profit share as agreed. Around 1992, citing Ditan Hospital's breach of contract by further transferring the "84" Disinfectant technology within the area north of the Yangtze River in Jiangsu Province and Nanjing City, Jinhu Chemical Plant ceased paying product profit shares to Ditan Hospital. On July 2, 1992, Jinhu Chemical Plant formed a joint venture with Hong Kong Li Qiang Co., Ltd. to establish Aitefu Health Products Company, which produced and sold "84" Disinfectant.

Aitefu Health Products Company obtained a hygiene permit for producing 84 Disinfectant from the Jiangsu Provincial Health Department in July 1994, which was renewed in August 1997. In October 1999, the company's "Aitefu '84' Disinfectant" obtained the hygiene permit approval document for domestic disinfectants and disinfection devices from the Ministry of Health. Aitefu Health Products Company's advertising investment in "Aitefu '84' Disinfectant" increased year by year.

On August 29, 1996, Aitefu Health Products Company applied to the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Office) for registration of the "84" trademark in Class 5 goods. Upon examination, the Trademark Office found that the trademark indicated the model and characteristics of the goods and rejected Aitefu Health Products Company's registration application in August 1997.

On January 29, 1999, Long'an Company, funded by Ditan Hospital, also applied to the Trademark Office for registration of the "Long'an 84" trademark in Class 5 disinfectants. Because "84" in the trademark directly indicated the model characteristics of the goods, the Trademark Office issued an examination opinion to Long'an Company on April 8, 1999, requiring the applicant to amend the application. Since Long'an Company made no amendments, the registration application was rejected by the Trademark Office.

This Court also found: In March 1999, Ditan Hospital applied to the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Review Board) for revocation of the Trademark Registration Certificate No. 1104561 for the "84" trademark in Class 5 goods (disinfectants) that had been erroneously issued to Aitefu Health Products Company. In its application, Ditan Hospital stated: The "84" Disinfectant technology has been transferred to 38 domestic enterprises and holds an important place in the disinfectant market; such products are collectively referred to as "84 Disinfectant".

In that application, Ditan Hospital also admitted that it had registered the "Long'an" trademark for "84" Disinfectant, and each transferee enterprise had also registered its own trademark. One transferee, Wuhan Qiaokou Yangzi Detergent Factory, applied to the Trademark Office on April 29, 1990, to register the "84" trademark in Class 5 goods, which was rejected by the Trademark Office based on Article 8, Paragraph 1, Item (5) of the Trademark Law, which prohibits the use of generic names and designs as trademarks.

On December 6, 1999, the Trademark Review Board issued the "Final Decision on the Reexamination of the Rejection of the '84' Trademark" (Shang Ping Zi (1999) No. 2750), rejecting Aitefu Health Products Company's reexamination application for registration of the "84" trademark in Class 5 disinfectant goods. The "Final Decision on the Reexamination of the Rejection of the '84' Trademark" stated: Upon review, although the applied trademark "84" had some graphic variation, it was still clearly readable. Currently, there are other enterprises selling 84 Disinfectant on the market, and this designation has become a common name for such products; it should not be registered for exclusive use by a single enterprise. This decision has become legally effective.

This Court additionally found: On April 30, 2000, Ditan Hospital filed a complaint with the Fair Trade Bureau of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce regarding counterfeit products on the market, seeking protection of the reputation of "84" Disinfectant products. On May 30, 2000, the Fair Trade Bureau issued Letter No. 26 to the Fair Trade Bureaus (Economic Inspection Divisions) of the Shandong, Hebei, Henan, Jiangsu, and Hunan Provincial Administrations for Industry and Commerce, requesting them to organize investigations and, in accordance with the law, seriously investigate and punish acts counterfeiting "84" Disinfectant. Upon investigation, the various local administrations for industry and commerce had never, based on the above letter, investigated or punished Aitefu Health Products Company's production and sale of "Aitefu Brand '84' Disinfectant".

On April 11, 2001, the Ministry of Health issued the "Notice of the Ministry of Health on Issuing the Provisions on the Naming of Health-Related Products", setting forth requirements for the naming of health-related products, including disinfectants and disinfection devices. Article 4, Item (3) of the "Provisions on the Naming of Health-Related Products" stipulates that the naming of health-related products must comply with the following principles: the name shall consist of three parts: trademark name, generic name, and attribute name. As of September 2002, there were five "84" Disinfectant products that had obtained the hygiene permit approval documents from the Ministry of Health and were still within the validity period. In addition to Long'an Company's "Long'an Brand 84 Disinfectant" and Aitefu Health Products Company's "Aitefu Brand 84 Disinfectant", these included: Qingdao Jiandun Detergent Factory's "Jiandun Brand 84 Disinfectant", Anhui Bengbu Epidemic Prevention Products Factory's "Yakang Brand 84 Disinfectant", and Nanjing Jiangnan Disinfectant Factory's "Zhongzhi Brand 84 Disinfectant".

This Court holds: Although Ditan Hospital is not a direct producer or operator of "84" Disinfectant products, its funding source as a public institution is based on differential subsidies. Its entrustment of Long'an Company to produce and sell "84" Disinfectant does not violate national laws and regulations. The agreement between Ditan Hospital and Long'an Company that legal disputes arising in the production, research and development, and sale of "84" Disinfectant would be handled in the name of Ditan Hospital is lawful and valid. Therefore, Ditan Hospital lawfully enjoys the standing of plaintiff in this case. The appellant Aitefu Health Products Company's ground of appeal that Ditan Hospital lacks standing as a plaintiff lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

Pursuant to Article 5, Item (2) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, the unique name of a well-known product shall be protected by law; without permission, no one may use the unique name of another's well-known product. The "84" Disinfectant involved in this case is a well-known product, and both Ditan Hospital and Aitefu Health Products Company have no dispute on this point. However, the parties sharply disagree on whether "84" is the unique name of the product and whose business activities made "84" Disinfectant well-known, forming the main disputed issues in this case.

The so-called unique name of a well-known product refers to a product name that is not generic for related products, has distinctive features, and through use on the product, enables consumers to distinguish that product from similar products of other business operators. However, once registered as a trademark, it no longer has the attributes of a unique name of a well-known product, but instead acquires the exclusivity of a registered trademark right. A unique name is also relative to a generic name; a generic name cannot obtain the exclusive right to use a unique name of a well-known product. When determining a generic name, product names that have been listed in national or industry standards, specialized reference books, or dictionaries shall be recognized as generic names. Moreover, terms that have become established by common usage among industry operators and are widely used to indicate a certain type of product shall also be recognized as generic names for such products. In this case, since the appellee Ditan Hospital developed and researched "84" Hepatitis Wash-Disinfectant (later renamed "84" Disinfectant) in 1984, it transferred the technology to multiple enterprises nationwide, licensing them to produce and sell "84" Disinfectant. In the relevant technology transfer license contracts, there were no special provisions regarding the name "84". Consequently, "84" Disinfectant came to be widely used as the name for this type of product, and each transferee enterprise, while using the product name, marked its own respective trademark. Currently, on the hygiene permit approval documents obtained by enterprises producing and selling "84" Disinfectant in accordance with the "Provisions on the Naming of Health-Related Products" issued by the Ministry of Health, the product names are the combination of each producer's trademark and the words "84 Disinfectant". The name "'84' Disinfectant" alone can no longer distinguish the source of the product. The marker for distinguishing such products is the trademark of each manufacturer, not the product name "84 Disinfectant". Therefore, the claim by Ditan Hospital that "84 Disinfectant" is the unique name of its well-known product and thus exclusively owned by it is difficult to sustain.

In fact, both parties were well aware of the manner in which "84" was used as a trade name for disinfectant solutions, and both had applied to the Trademark Office to register "84" as a trademark for their exclusive use. It is particularly noteworthy that Ditan Hospital had previously applied to the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board to cancel the registration of the "84" trademark by others in Class 5 (disinfectant products) on the grounds that "84" was a generic name for disinfectant products. The acknowledgment by Ditan Hospital during the trademark registration dispute that "84" was a generic name for such products truthfully reflected the actual usage of the name "84," and it imposes a certain degree of binding effect on Ditan Hospital's subsequent retraction of that statement and its claim for infringement of its civil rights and interests based on the assertion that "84" is a distinctive name of a well-known product. Over the years, the Ministry of Health, which oversees the production and distribution of "84" disinfectant products, and the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board, which handles trademark registration disputes, have also managed "84" as a generic name for disinfectants or have determined that "84" reflects the model characteristics of the product and have thus refused to register it as a trademark. "84" disinfectant has been widely used as a product name generally accepted within the industry. In addition to the parties to this dispute, other enterprises have lawfully used this name with the approval of the national health administrative authorities. Therefore, the appellant, Aitefu Health Products Company's ground of appeal that "84" is a generic name for similar disinfectant products is established, and this court should support it.

In summary, the distinctive name of a well-known product is protected by law, and the right holder is entitled to prevent others from engaging in unfair competition by unauthorized use of such distinctive name. However, the "84" disinfectant involved in this case is not a distinctive name of a well-known product and cannot be exclusively used by any single entity. The original judgment was unclear in its factual findings on whether "84" disinfectant is a distinctive name of a well-known product and was erroneous in its application of law, and should be corrected. In order to resolve the dispute between the parties fairly and reasonably, this court made full efforts to mediate during the proceedings and provided the parties with an opportunity to settle the dispute through their own negotiation. However, the parties remained adamant in their respective positions and failed to reach an agreement. Therefore, pursuant to Article 5, Paragraph (2) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court hereby renders the following judgment:

1.  The Civil Judgment (2001) Gao Zhi Chu Zi No. 79 of the Beijing High People's Court is hereby reversed.

2.  The claims of Beijing Ditan Hospital are hereby dismissed.

The case acceptance fees for the first and second instances, totaling RMB 56,020, shall be borne by Beijing Ditan Hospital.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Jiang Zhipei

Acting Judge: Duan Lihong

Acting Judge: Xia Junli

March 23, 2003

Clerk: Li Jian
